integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the run's own application directory. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, public search, or unexplained network activity was detected.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Workflow: 98 file changes, 16 build/test/browser verification actions.

overall.summary: The deeper of the two inboxes: a multi-window compose deck, a rich-text editor, a settings surface and a shortcuts dialog, on top of the largest seeded mailbox here. No tests.

standards.summary: 10,774 lines across 44 files with a real separation between store, selectors, mutations and views, spoiled only by the absence of any automated coverage.

findings.title: No automated tests on a mutation-heavy application
findings.detail: Archiving, labelling, starring, snoozing, sending and draft persistence all mutate a shared store, and none of it is covered. src/lib/mutations.ts and src/lib/selectors.ts are pure and testable as written. Cover the label and snooze paths at minimum.

findings.title: Seed data is a 1,435-line module
findings.detail: src/data/threads.ts holds the whole mailbox as one literal. It is legible, but a per-category split would let the search and label fixtures be reused in tests without importing the entire corpus.

strengths: store/, hooks/, data/, lib/ and components/ each own one concern
selectors.ts and mutations.ts keep read and write paths apart
43 memoisation sites on a list that renders 48 threads with live filtering

specification.summary: Every essential outcome is present, and the product-depth section is answered with genuine extras rather than decorative controls.
strengths: Multi-window compose deck with draft persistence and a rich-text editor
Settings view, keyboard-shortcuts dialog, snooze menu and label menu all functional
Category tabs, bulk selection toolbar, importance markers and attachment indicators
Storage meter and label counts wired to the seeded corpus rather than hardcoded

ux.summary: Density, alignment and the toolbar hierarchy read as Gmail on sight. The 48-thread inbox gives the list enough material to feel like a real mailbox.

findings.title: Thread list has no date grouping
findings.detail: 48 threads run as one continuous list with only per-row timestamps. The sibling run's TODAY / YESTERDAY / LAST 7 DAYS headers make a long list scannable at a glance. Add date separators.

findings.title: Brand mark is a generic envelope
findings.detail: The header uses a blue envelope glyph rather than a Gmail-style mark, which is the one place the visual quotation falls short. Cosmetic only.

strengths: Row density and column rhythm match the reference closely
Label chips inline with the subject, exactly as in the product
Snooze and follow-up affordances visible without opening a thread
Responsive shell holds together at mobile widths
